measures.title: Amend Corvallis Charter to change city council, wards, and terms
measures.summary: Referred by the Corvallis City Council on the recommendation of its Charter Review Task Force, this would amend sections 8, 9 and 10 of the city charter. It would cut the number of city councilors and wards from nine to six, lengthen councilor terms from two to four years with staggered elections, and limit councilors and the mayor to three consecutive terms. All six councilors would be elected in November 2028 under the new structure, with odd-numbered wards serving an initial two-year term.
measures.yesMeans: Corvallis would move to six wards and six councilors with staggered four-year terms, and councilors and the mayor would be limited to three consecutive terms.
measures.noMeans: Corvallis would keep nine wards and nine councilors with two-year terms and no term limits.
